drills.q: Pick and defend a North Star for a tutoring platform.
drills.a: Weekly active learners completing an assessed activity (value received, sum-form, plausible renewal link). Reject logins (activity), courses completed (quantity-gaming), DAU/MAU (ratio). Close with cohort validation that high-NS quarters preceded higher renewal.

drills.q: Write two guardrail thresholds for a ranking-model change.
drills.a: E.g., p95 latency <= baseline + 10%; relevance score >= -1% vs control; complaint/flag rate <0.5% of sessions; next-7-day return non-negative within noise. Thresholds set from historical variance, signed off BEFORE results exist.

drills.q: Compute downstream impact: activation moves 28% -> 34%. Relative lift on everything after?
drills.a: 6pts / 28% ~= 21.4% relative increase in activated users, multiplying every later stage's volume proportionally. That leverage is why activation usually beats retention polish when the retention curve already flattens.

drills.q: Build the metric tree for an enterprise LMS (Cornerstone-style) with renewal-revenue outcome.
drills.a: NS: weekly active learners completing >=1 assessed activity. Inputs: new-seat activation <=7 days, manager-assigned coverage, median weekly minutes/active learner, W8 return rate. Guardrails: course-quality rating >=4.0/5, compliance-deadline miss rate falling, tickets per 1K learners. Each input gets SQL-exact definition to kill definition disputes.

drills.q: Growth wants signups; infra wants cost/user down. Resolve without seniority.
drills.a: Escalate to shared parent units: marginal NS value per signup (cohort LTV by channel) vs cost per user; set a written exchange rate in planning - accept paid signups while CAC payback <=12 months and gross margin >=75%. Conflicting local optima are normal; resolving by unwritten vibes is not.

drills.q: Month one of a new AI tutoring feature: what do you instrument, what do you defer?
drills.a: Instrument only: outcome (% hint-sessions ending in independent correct solution <24h), inputs (hint-request rate, post-hint success), guardrails (over-reliance flag >70% hint-attempts, token cost/session), weekly cohort readout. Defer NPS/referral/trees until behavior stabilizes ~week 6-8. Attention bandwidth is the constraint, not storage.

drills.q: Design a Goodhart stress test for 'minutes practiced' as headline.
drills.a: Ask how the number could rise while reality doesn't: idle-session stuffing, autoplay grinding, repeat-easy-content farming. Attach counter-metrics (checkpoint pass rate, next-day return, content diversity floor) and run net arithmetic: headline gain minus weighted guardrail losses; if net ~0 it's grind, iterate rather than celebrate.

drills.q: Post-iOS14.5, why distrust channel-level ROI dashboards and what replaces them?
drills.a: Identifier loss makes last-click attribution systematically wrong and walled gardens double-count conversions. Replace with incrementality testing (geo holdouts, conversion-lift studies) plus first-party behavioral proxies; treat platform-reported ROAS as directional and say so in writing.

drills.q: Execs want one number on the dashboard. What goes up and what must accompany it?
drills.a: One output-form NS + 2-3 inputs + 1-2 guardrails as sparklines vs targets, with mandatory anomaly annotation within a day and a two-click drill-down (NS -> inputs -> segments/experiments) built before accepting the slot - owning the question chain keeps the number yours.

drills.q: A marketplace has supply-side and demand-side health pulling apart. One North Star?
drills.a: Prefer TWO explicit stars balanced deliberately (e.g., bookings AND host earnings) over one number pretending the tension away - forcing one invites optimizing the easier side into imbalance. If leadership insists on one, use a bounded composite with publicly agreed weights and monitor both components separately for divergence.
